title: Development and validation of venous thrombosis risk prediction model and scale for lung cancer patients in intensive care unit based on interpretable machine learning.
summary: An interpretable model predicted venous-thrombosis risk among lung-cancer patients in ICU.
ai_technology: Boruta, variance-inflation analysis and LASSO screened predictors; nine models, including CatBoost, estimated ICU venous-thromboembolism risk, with SHAP interpretation and a score derived from the best model.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: In 3,694 ICU records across MIMIC-IV, eICU and NWICU, CatBoost AUCs were 0.7648 in training, 0.6437 in internal validation, 0.6822 in eICU and 0.7153 in NWICU. This retrospective prediction does not establish clinical benefit.
evidence.unknown: The cohort is drawn from existing ICU databases; reported validation AUCs are modest (0.64–0.72), and no prospective clinical-impact evaluation is reported.
evidence.ai_role: Boruta, variance-inflation analysis and LASSO screened predictors; nine models, including CatBoost, estimated ICU venous-thromboembolism risk, with SHAP interpretation and a score derived from the best model.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
